section_name: Additive Offset Adjustment and Intercept Recalibration under Squared Error Loss

candidates.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine
candidates.reason: Provides the foundational additive stagewise formulation where the initial baseline predictor is determined by minimizing squared error loss via a constant additive offset, yielding the sample mean, and subsequent stages fit fixed residuals.

candidates.title: A calibration hierarchy for risk models was defined: from utopia to empirical data
candidates.reason: Formulates the canonical hierarchy of predictive recalibration, formally defining Level 1 calibration (mean calibration / calibration-in-the-large) as adjusting solely an additive intercept while keeping the underlying predictor completely fixed.

candidates.title: Updating methods improved the performance of a clinical prediction model in new patients
candidates.reason: Directly analyzes intercept updating (recalibration-in-the-large) holding the predictor fixed as an offset variable, demonstrating that an additive constant adjustment corrects systematic mean prediction error without modifying predictor discrimination.

candidates.title: Validation and updating of predictive logistic regression models: a study on sample size and shrinkage
candidates.reason: Examines the mathematics and sample size implications of adjusting only the intercept parameter while holding the linear predictor fixed, proving that this isolates and corrects constant baseline shift.

candidates.title: A closed testing procedure to select an appropriate method for updating a prediction model
candidates.reason: Presents a formal statistical framework testing whether updating only the additive intercept while constraining the predictor slope to unity suffices to remove systematic prediction bias.

candidates.title: Partial Time Regressions as Compared with Individual Trends
candidates.reason: Establishes the seminal Frisch-Waugh theorem showing that partialling out a constant intercept term under least squares is mathematically identical to subtracting the sample mean of the residuals.

candidates.title: Seasonal Adjustment of Economic Time Series and Multiple Regression Analysis
candidates.reason: Generalizes the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem, proving algebraically that least-squares projection onto a constant vector forces the sample mean of the residual errors to exactly zero.

candidates.title: Generalized Linear Models
candidates.reason: Introduces the formal mathematical formulation of an offset term (a predictor component with a fixed unit coefficient) and demonstrates that fitting an intercept with an identity link minimizes squared error by estimating the mean residual.

candidates.title: A New Vector Partition of the Probability Score
candidates.reason: Derives the algebraic decomposition of mean squared error into calibration/reliability and resolution components, showing analytically that an additive prediction shift directly eliminates the calibration error component.

candidates.title: Neural Networks and the Bias/Variance Dilemma
candidates.reason: Provides the foundational bias-variance decomposition under squared error loss, showing that a fixed, uniform prediction error acts as an isolated additive bias term that can be eliminated without altering predictor variance.

candidates.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression
candidates.reason: Formulates post-hoc recalibration techniques for continuous regression settings, holding the underlying predictor fixed while updating output parameters to align predictions with empirical observation.

candidates.title: Evaluating and Calibrating Uncertainty Prediction in Regression Tasks
candidates.reason: Investigates regression recalibration under squared error and residual variance evaluation, analyzing post-processing adjustments applied to fixed predictor outputs.

candidates.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
candidates.reason: Systematically compares post-processing calibration functions where underlying representations or predictor outputs remain frozen, evaluating affine transformations that include additive intercept shifts.

candidates.title: Predicting Good Probabilities With Supervised Learning
candidates.reason: Analyzes post-hoc calibration methods holding model predictions fixed, evaluating squared error (Brier score) improvements achieved by fitting intercept and scaling parameters on validation sets.
